hook: What 420 feet of icebreaker does to Arctic ice.
narration: This is what four hundred twenty feet of icebreaker does to Arctic sea ice.
The Coast Guard Cutter Healy, in the Beaufort Sea, on September first, two thousand twenty one.
On the bridge, ice pilot Ensign Valarie Hines steered the ship through the floes.
An icebreaker's rounded bow rides up onto the ice sheet, and the weight of the whole ship crushes it from above.
In two thousand eighteen, Healy was one of just two icebreakers in U.S. service.
Slabs of broken ice tumbled along the red hull and churned in the wake.
outcome: Hines broke the Healy through the Arctic ice and on across the Beaufort Sea.
title: Icebreaker crushes Arctic sea ice
description:
Ice pilot Ens. Valarie Hines breaks the Coast Guard Cutter Healy through Arctic sea ice in the Beaufort Sea on Sept. 1, 2021.

extra_sources.excerpt: The Healy is a 420-foot medium icebreaker, homeported in Seattle.  As one of two icebreakers in U.S. service, the Healy is the only icebreaker dedicated to scientific research in the Arctic.
